videos.title: What Is the Firmament? Let. Scripture. Speak | Semitic Jew | S3 E4
videos.description:
What does Scripture mean when it says God created “the heaven and the earth”? What is the firmament, what did it divide, and why did God call it Heaven?

In Season 3, Episode 4, we continue our examination of Genesis by allowing Scripture to interpret Scripture. We compare Genesis with passages throughout the Old Testament, Apocrypha, and New Testament to examine:

• The heaven and earth of Genesis 1:1  
• The waters above and below the firmament  
• Why the firmament was called Heaven  
• The sun, moon, stars, and birds in relation to heaven  
• The windows of heaven and fountains of the deep  
• The distinction between what Scripture states, what logically follows, and what remains a question  

Primary passages include Genesis 1:1, 6–8, 14–20; Genesis 7:11–12; Genesis 8:2; Job 37:18; Psalms 19:1, 33:6–9, 104:2, and 148:1–6; Isaiah 40:22; Ezekiel 1:22–26; Ecclesiasticus 43; and 2 Corinthians 12:2–4.

Read what God said. Follow the language. Compare the passages. Then test every conclusion against Scripture.

videos.title: Nolan Wells Update: Are We Being Gaslight.. Again? | Semitic Jew
videos.description:
They’ve told us their conclusion. Now show us how they got there.

In this video, I examine the Nolan Wells grand jury report, the family counsel’s statements about injury timing, and the reasoning behind the public narrative.

We examine:
• What “undetermined” and “consistent with drowning” actually establish.
• The reported fall and the unanswered question of what caused the head injury.
• Counsel’s account of Dr. Mitchell’s findings.
• What GPS data and witness testimony corroborate.
• Why official conclusions must remain open to careful examination.

The central question: Does the certainty of the public narrative exceed what the evidence establishes?

Watch, examine the sources, and share your questions in the comments.

videos.title: The First Day: Genesis 1:1–5 | Semitic Jew | S3 E3
videos.description:
Link to Previous Episode: https://youtu.be/h2DFf0AeGJk

What happened on the first day of creation? Does Genesis describe a continuous account, or is a gap being inserted between its opening verses?

In Season 3, Episode 3, Semitic examines Genesis 1:1–5 and presents the case for reading all five verses as the first day. We follow the passage’s sequence, compare Scripture with Scripture, and examine the assumptions behind gap theory and attempts to place millions of years within the account.

In this lesson:
• “In the beginning” and the creation of heaven and earth.
• What “without form, and void” describes.
• Darkness, the deep, and the Spirit of God.
• “Let there be light.”
• Why God calls the light Day and the darkness Night.
• How evening and morning complete the first day.

Bring your Bible, follow the reasoning, and examine the words for yourself.

videos.title: How Do We Study Scripture? Let Scripture Speak | Semitic Jew | S3 E2
videos.description:
Episode 3 Link :  https://youtu.be/X11Jb9HLZkQ

How do we distinguish what Scripture actually says from what we bring to it?

In Season 3, Episode 2 of the Semitic Jew Podcast, we establish a practical method for studying Scripture carefully. We examine understanding, context, translation, literary form, cross-references, inference, historical tools, and obedience.

This lesson also demonstrates why words such as “saints” and “world” must be interpreted according to their surrounding passages—not religious assumptions.

Scriptures examined include Nehemiah 8:8, Acts 8:30–35, Exodus 3:7–15, Luke 24:27, Acts 17:11, Psalm 50:5, Psalm 148:14, Romans 15:25–27, Isaiah 45:17, John 17:9–18, Proverbs 18:13, James 1:22–25, and more.

The six-step study method:

1. Read the passage.
2. Identify its context.
3. Explain its words.
4. Compare relevant passages.
5. Test your conclusion.
6. Apply what you learn.

Next episode: Genesis 1:1.

videos.title: Who Is God? Let Scripture Speak | Semitic Jew | S3 E1
videos.description:
Episode 2 Link : https://youtu.be/NK6m4JjLviI

Everybody has something to say about God. But how much of what we believe comes from Scripture—and how much have we inherited without examining it?

In Season 3, Episode 1, Semitic opens the Old Testament, Apocrypha, and New Testament to examine one foundational question: Who is God according to Scripture?

We begin with the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: his identity, his covenant, his character, and what knowing him requires of us.

In this lesson:
• God as Creator and giver of life.
• His name and covenant with Israel.
• The living, eternal God.
• Why human-made images cannot establish God’s identity.
• His mercy, justice, faithfulness, and holiness.
• The connection between knowing God and keeping his commandments.

Bring your Bible, take notes, and read each passage in context.

After time away because of work and life's responsibilities, I’m returning with a clear mission: teach the Bible carefully, reason clearly, and build a library of lessons you can revisit.

In Episode 00, I explain where I’ve been, thank the supporters who make this ministry possible, and outline what’s coming: studies beginning in Genesis, historical context, maps, sources beyond the Bible, and weekly live discussions.

We’ll examine what Scripture says, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and ask serious questions about the arguments people make for—and against—the Bible.
